question: What colour marks a work zone sign?
choices: Orange, with messages in black letters
Yellow, with messages in black letters
Red, with messages in white letters
Green, with messages in white letters
explanation: Work zones are usually marked with orange warning signs. The orange signs with messages in black letters identify work zones and direct drivers as they travel through them. When you see these signs, go on high alert and follow their directions.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Yellow signs are permanent warning signs.
Red with white lettering is used for stop signs and prohibitions.
Green with white lettering is used for guidance signs.

question: This sign shows a worker and has small orange flags mounted above its upper corners. What does that combination tell you?
choices: Workers are present on the site right now and are at risk of being struck
Work is scheduled to begin at this location next week
The work zone has ended
A survey crew is measuring the road
explanation: Human activity signs are those with a symbol of a person. They are only used when the workplace is active — people are working and at risk of being struck. Red or orange flags are used on human activity signs when they are displayed close to the ground. Driving mistakes here have the potential to cause fatal injuries to road workers.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Human activity signs are removed or covered when no one is working.
The end of a work zone is signed END CONSTRUCTION.
Survey work has its own human activity sign.

question: You see this sign approaching a work zone. What should you expect?
choices: A traffic control person may stop you with a Stop/Slow paddle — adjust your speed gradually to avoid rear-end collisions
A police checkpoint ahead
A pedestrian crossing ahead
A crossing guard for a school ahead
explanation: Traffic control persons actively manage traffic past the workplace using Stop/Slow paddles. Traffic may be required to stop, so adjust your speed gradually to avoid rear-end collisions. Respect road workers and follow their directions — you are travelling through their workplace.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Police checkpoints are not signed with orange work-zone signs.
Pedestrian crossings use a different sign showing a walking figure.
School crossing guards are associated with school-area signs, not orange work-zone signs.

question: What does this sign tell you?
choices: Construction activities begin 1.5 km ahead — choose a different route or be prepared for delays
Construction has finished 1.5 km back
The speed limit is 1.5 km/h
The work zone is 1.5 km long
explanation: This is an advance temporary condition sign: construction activities will begin 1.5 km ahead. Choose a different route or be prepared for delays. Advance signs with distances are used when drivers need time to prepare for conditions ahead.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The end of a work zone is signed END CONSTRUCTION.
The figure is a distance, not a speed.
The distance is to the start of the work, not its length.

question: What does this sign mean?
choices: The road has returned to normal — expect no more impact from road work
Construction begins at this point
The road is permanently closed ahead
Construction is suspended for the day
explanation: This sign means the road has returned to normal and you should expect no more impact from road work. Where the end point of a project is obvious, this sign is not often used.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The start of construction is signed with advance temporary condition signs.
A permanent closure would be signed and barricaded.
The sign marks the physical end of the work zone, not a schedule.

question: What hazard does this work-zone sign warn about?
choices: A difference in elevation between the lanes — a tyre catching the edge could cause a loss of control
The road narrows but keeps the same number of lanes
Loose gravel that may be thrown up by other vehicles
A steep hill within the work zone
explanation: This sign warns of a difference in elevation between the lanes. A tyre catching the edge could cause a vehicle to lose control. Change lanes deliberately and squarely rather than drifting across the lip.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A narrowing without a change in lane count has its own sign.
Loose or rutted surfaces have a separate road-surface-conditions sign.
The stepped profile shows a height difference between lanes, not a gradient.

question: A flashing light unit at a work zone displays a single arrow pointing left. What does it mean?
choices: The lane ahead is closed or obstructed — move over, passing only on the side the arrow indicates
Traffic may pass on either side of the unit
Traffic must stop at the unit
The unit is in caution mode and no lane is closed
explanation: A flashing light unit displaying a left or right arrow means the lane ahead is closed and you will have to move over, or there is an obstruction you will have to drive around. When a single arrow head is displayed, it is safe to pass the unit but only on the side indicated by the arrow.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Passing on either side is safe only when TWO arrow heads are displayed at the same time.
The unit directs traffic around a closure; it does not require a stop.
Caution mode is shown by lamps in a straight line or bar — and even then, it does not indicate that it is safe to pass.

question: A flashing light unit shows its lamps in a straight line or bar. What does this 'caution' mode indicate?
choices: A hazard such as a vehicle occupying a lane or workers laying out signs — it does NOT indicate that it is safe to pass
It is safe to pass on either side
The lane ahead is closed
The work zone has ended
explanation: Lamps in a straight line or bar is called 'caution' mode. It is used to alert drivers to a hazard, such as a vehicle occupying a lane or workers laying out signs. The unit in caution mode does not indicate that it is safe to pass — drivers must evaluate the situation and decide based on the conditions present.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Two arrow heads displayed together is what indicates it is safe to pass on either side.
A closed lane is indicated by an arrow, not a bar.
The end of the work zone is signed END CONSTRUCTION.

subtopic: do not pass in a work zone
question: A Do Not Pass sign is posted in a work zone before a merge point. What is its status?
choices: It is a regulatory sign — disobeying it is an offence that warrants a ticket
It is advisory only within a work zone
It applies only when workers are present
It applies only to commercial vehicles
explanation: Do Not Pass is used to create an orderly flow of traffic before a merge point, or to prevent passing where it is unsafe. This is a regulatory sign — you must obey its message, and disobeying it is an offence that warrants a ticket. Obeying it at merge points makes work zones safer.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The handbook is explicit that this is a regulatory sign, not advice.
The prohibition does not depend on whether workers are visible.
It applies to all drivers.

question: What does this sign tell you?
choices: Construction is ahead — prepare for unusual road conditions and traffic moving at different speeds
Workers are on the site at this moment
The road ahead is closed to all traffic
A survey crew is working beside the road
explanation: General work-zone signs warn of unusual conditions and prepare you for construction traffic that may be moving at a different speed. They remain in place until the road is returned to normal — unlike human activity signs, which are used only when workers are actually present.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Signs indicating that workers are present carry red or orange flags and are removed when the site is inactive.
A full closure would be barricaded and signed as such.
Survey work has its own specific human activity sign.

question: What does this work-zone sign tell you about the road ahead?
choices: Tar has been sprayed and the surface may be slippery
The road has just been swept and is clear
Loose gravel has been spread across the surface
A lane is closed while lines are being painted
explanation: Tar has been sprayed on the road ahead. It can make the surface slippery, and spray thrown up by tyres can stick tar to your vehicle. Slow down, keep well back, or choose another route.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The sign warns of a hazard on the surface, not of work already finished.
Loose surface material is covered by a different work-zone sign.
Lane closures are shown by lane-control and arrow devices.

question: You are in the right lane and see this work-zone sign. Why does the handbook say to merge as soon as it is safe?
choices: Merging late is an offence that carries demerit points
Forming the single lane early avoids conflict at the last moment
The right lane reopens once the work zone ends
Drivers in the left lane must give way to you
explanation: The sign gives advance notice that the right lane ends, so traffic can form a single lane in plenty of time. Merging early spreads the movement out instead of forcing vehicles together at the last possible moment. It is often posted with a Do Not Pass sign for the same reason.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The handbook gives a safety reason for merging early, not a penalty.
What happens beyond the work zone does not change the need to merge now.
Merging drivers fit into gaps in the through lane; the other lane is not obliged to yield.

question: What should you expect after passing this work-zone sign?
choices: A stop sign posted at the end of the work zone
The road ahead closed, so you must turn back
Traffic signals controlling the work zone
Traffic may be stopped ahead by a traffic control person
explanation: This sign is advance notice that traffic may be stopped ahead by a traffic control person using a stop/slow paddle. Ease off gradually rather than braking hard, so the driver behind you is not caught out.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: The sign warns of a person directing traffic, not of a permanent stop sign.
A closed road is signed as a closure with a detour.
Work zones are controlled by people and devices rather than by traffic signals.

question: What does this work-zone sign warn about?
choices: A difference in height between the lanes
The surface may be rutted or grooved
Fresh tar sprayed across the surface
The road narrows without losing a lane
explanation: The surface ahead may be rutted, grooved or otherwise unsound. Two-wheeled traffic is most at risk — a bicycle or motorcycle can become unstable on a grooved surface — so slow down and leave riders extra room.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A step in height between lanes has its own uneven-lanes sign.
Fresh tar is shown by a separate sign carrying the word TAR.
A narrowing that keeps the same lane count has its own sign.

question: What does this work-zone sign tell you about the lanes ahead?
choices: The lanes shift sideways around the work area
One lane ends, so traffic has to merge
The road narrows but keeps the same number of lanes
Two-way traffic begins on a single carriageway
explanation: The road ahead narrows, but you keep the same number of lanes — there is simply less width in each one. Slow down and keep central in your lane; a lane-ends sign is used when a lane is actually lost.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A lateral shift is shown by a different work-zone device.
That is the lane-ends sign, which shows one lane tapering away.
Two-way traffic on one carriageway has its own sign.

question: What does this work-zone sign warn you about?
choices: Construction vehicles may enter or leave on the right
A construction zone begins 1.5 kilometres ahead
Workers are on foot on the road surface ahead
The right lane is closed for construction work
explanation: Construction traffic may be turning in or pulling out on the right, and those vehicles are often moving much more slowly than through traffic. Differences in speed are the main hazard in a work zone, so ease off early. A matching sign is used where the entrance is on the left.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Distance to a work zone is given by the construction-ahead sign with a distance on it.
Workers on foot are shown by a human-activity sign.
Lane closures are signed separately.

question: What does this work-zone sign mean, and what may you be asked to do?
choices: Rock has fallen on the road and a lane is blocked
Blasting is under way nearby and traffic may have to stop
A quarry entrance is ahead and trucks are turning
Heavy equipment is crossing the road ahead
explanation: Blasting is taking place on or near the road, and traffic may be required to stop while it happens. Debris can be thrown by a blast and the noise can startle a driver. The sign is normally used together with the Shut Off Your Radio Transmitter sign and an End Blasting Zone sign.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Fallen rock is a different hazard with its own warning.
Vehicles joining the road are covered by the construction-traffic sign.
Equipment crossing is signed separately where it applies.

question: What activity does this work-zone sign tell you is happening beside the road?
choices: A traffic control person is directing traffic
Work is going on overhead on cables
A road-maintenance vehicle is sweeping the shoulder
A survey crew is working on or near the road
explanation: This is a human-activity sign showing a survey crew at work on or beside the road. Human-activity signs are posted only while workers are actually present, so treat them as a signal that people are on the site right now and a driving mistake could injure someone.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A traffic control person is shown by a sign with a stop/slow paddle.
Overhead cable work has its own human-activity sign.
Maintenance vehicles are covered by other work-zone signs.

question: What does this work-zone sign warn you about?
choices: Work going on overhead on electrical or data cables
A low bridge that limits the height of vehicles
Overhead lane signals controlling the lanes ahead
A crane lifting loads from one side to the other
explanation: Workers are above the road, working on electrical or data cables. It is a human-activity sign, so it is posted only while people are on the site. Slow down, expect equipment near the roadway, and give the crew room.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Height restrictions are shown by a low-clearance sign giving the headroom.
Overhead lane-control signals are a permanent installation, not a work-zone sign.
The sign covers cable work rather than lifting operations.

question: A flashing light unit in a work zone displays two arrow heads at the same time. What does that tell you?
choices: You must pass the unit on the left only
The unit is in caution mode, so passing may not be safe
The lane ahead is closed and you may pass on either side
The lane ahead is open and no change is needed
explanation: Two arrow heads shown together mean the lane ahead is closed, or something is blocking it, and it is safe to pass the unit on either side. A single arrow would mean you may pass only on the side the arrow points to, and lamps in a straight bar is caution mode, which does not tell you it is safe to pass at all.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A single arrow head restricts you to one side; two arrows do not.
Caution mode shows the lamps in a straight line or bar, not as arrows.
The unit is only used when the lane ahead is closed or obstructed.

question: What do guidance signs look like, and what do they do?
choices: Rectangular, usually green with white letters — they provide information and directions, including route numbers and distances
Diamond-shaped and yellow — they warn of conditions ahead
Octagonal and red — they require you to stop
Rectangular and orange — they mark temporary conditions
explanation: Guidance signs are rectangular, usually with a green background and white letters. They provide information and directions, including route numbers and distances. Other signs with different colours guide you to facilities, services and attractions.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Yellow diamonds are warning signs.
The octagon is reserved for stop signs.
Orange marks work zones.

question: What does this route marker tell you about the road?
choices: It is a provincial 100-series highway with controlled access
It is a municipal street in Halifax
It is a gravel road maintained seasonally
It is a private road
explanation: Highway 102 is a provincial highway with controlled access, also referred to as a 100-series highway. Access is permitted only at specially designed intersections called interchanges, which is why they need acceleration and deceleration lanes.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Municipal streets are signed with street-name signs.
Road surface is not indicated by a route marker.
100-series highways are public provincial roads.

question: You see a rectangular sign in a colour other than green — for example blue or brown. What is it most likely doing?
choices: Guiding you to facilities, services or attractions
Warning you of a hazard ahead
Setting a speed limit for a special zone
Marking a work zone
explanation: Guidance signs are rectangular, usually green with white letters, and give routes, directions and distances. Signs of other colours in the same family guide you to facilities, services and attractions rather than telling you what you must do.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Hazards are warned about with yellow diamonds.
Speed limits are set on white rectangular regulatory signs.
Work zones use orange signs.

question: A green sign reads 'Halifax 12 km'. What does the number tell you?
choices: The remaining distance to that destination
The speed limit for the next section of road
The exit number for Halifax
The number of the highway you are joining
explanation: Guidance signs provide information and directions, including route numbers and distances. On a destination sign the figure beside a place name is how far away it is.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Speed limits appear on white regulatory signs reading MAXIMUM.
Exit numbers are shown on separate exit signage.
Route numbers appear inside a shield-shaped route marker.

question: You are approaching an interchange on a controlled-access highway. What will the signs there tell you, and what is always required?
choices: Whether to merge, yield or stop — and in every case you must yield to through traffic until there is a safe gap
Only the name of the road you are joining; through traffic must make room for you
The speed you must maintain through the interchange, with no yielding required
Nothing useful — interchanges are unsigned
explanation: Signs will be posted to inform you whether to merge, yield or stop. In all these situations you are required to yield to through traffic until a safe gap can be identified before entering the highway. Give careful attention to the directions on the signs leading up to the interchange.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Traffic already on the highway has priority; you must find the gap.
Interchange signs govern how you join, not a mandatory speed, and yielding is always required.
Interchanges are extensively signed precisely because two groups of drivers are changing speed at once.

question: You are in a lane with this sign posted over it. What must you do at the intersection?
choices: Turn right — you may only turn right from this lane
Turn right or go straight through
Turn right only if the light is green
Merge right before the intersection
explanation: A right turn only lane sign indicates to drivers approaching an intersection in the designated lane that they must only turn right from that lane. Going straight from a turn-only lane cuts across drivers who correctly expect you to turn.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A lane permitting both movements would show two arrows.
The lane restriction applies regardless of the signal.
The sign governs your movement at the intersection, not a lane change before it.

question: What movements are permitted from a lane marked with this sign?
choices: Straight through or a left turn
A left turn only
Straight through only
Any movement, including a right turn
explanation: This sign indicates to drivers approaching an intersection in the designated lane that they must only proceed straight through or turn left.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A left-turn-only lane would show a single left arrow.
A straight-only lane would show a single upward arrow.
A right turn is not among the permitted movements.

question: This sign is posted over the centre lane of a multi-lane road. What is that lane for?
choices: Left-turning vehicles from both directions only — never for passing
Passing slower traffic in either direction
An extra through lane in the direction of heaviest traffic
Emergency vehicles only
explanation: This sign indicates that the designated lane is reserved for left-turning vehicles only, shared by traffic travelling in both directions. Never use this lane to pass or overtake another vehicle, and do not drive in it for an extended distance.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Using it to pass puts you head-on into a driver entering from the other direction.
That describes a lane controlled by overhead lane-control signals, which is a different arrangement.
It is not an emergency lane.

question: What do yellow lines and white lines each tell you about the traffic beside them?
choices: Yellow lines separate lanes moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction
Yellow lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; white lines separate opposing traffic
Yellow lines mark the edge of the road; white lines mark the centre
The colours are interchangeable and carry no meaning
explanation: Yellow lines separate travel lanes moving in opposite directions. White lines separate travel lanes moving in the same direction. Single solid white lines are used as right-edge lines, and single solid yellow lines as left-edge lines on divided highways — so if you see the reverse, you are travelling in the wrong direction.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: This reverses the meaning of the two colours.
Both colours are used for edge lines and for lane separation, depending on the direction of adjacent traffic.
The colours carry specific, distinct meanings.

question: What do these pavement markings mean?
choices: You cannot cross them to pass in either direction
Passing with care is permitted in both directions
Passing is permitted only from the right-hand lane
The lanes travel in the same direction
explanation: When the centre line consists of continuous double solid yellow lines, you cannot cross them to pass in either direction.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: That is the meaning of a broken yellow centre line.
Passing permission depends on which side has the broken line, and here neither does.
Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

question: What do these pavement markings mean?
choices: Passing with care is permitted in both directions
Passing is prohibited in both directions
The road is one-way
The lane to the right is a turning lane
explanation: A yellow dotted or broken line is used as the centre line on a two-lane, two-way road where passing with care is permitted in both directions. 'With care' still means you need clear sight distance and a safe gap.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: A prohibition would be shown by a solid line on your side.
Yellow lines indicate traffic moving in opposite directions, so the road is two-way.
Turning lanes are marked with arrows and signs.

question: The centre line shows a solid yellow line on your side and a broken yellow line on the other side. May you pass?
choices: No — passing with care is permitted only if the broken line is on your side
Yes, because one of the lines is broken
Yes, but only if oncoming traffic is not visible
Yes, if you can complete the pass within 150 metres
explanation: On a two-lane road, passing with care is permitted if the broken yellow line is on your side of the centreline markings. A solid line in your lane combined with a broken line in the approaching lane is one of the places the handbook lists where passing is always unsafe and usually illegal.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: It matters which side the broken line is on — it grants permission only to the traffic beside it.
The solid line usually marks a place with inadequate sight distance, which is precisely why you cannot see whether it is clear.
Distance does not override the marking.

question: What do these pavement markings tell you?
choices: The lanes carry traffic moving in the same direction, and the solid white lines are the road edges
The lanes carry traffic moving in opposite directions
Passing is prohibited
The road is a two-way left turn lane
explanation: White lines separate travel lanes moving in the same direction. Single solid white lines are used as right-edge lines along the roadway and for guiding traffic travelling in the same direction.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Opposing traffic is separated by yellow lines.
A broken white line permits lane changes.
A two-way left turn lane is marked with double lines and signed with opposing left arrows.

question: You are driving on a divided highway and notice a solid WHITE line on your left and a solid YELLOW line on your right. What does this tell you?
choices: You are travelling in the wrong direction
You are in a passing lane
You are approaching an exit ramp
You are on a two-way road
explanation: Single solid white lines are used as right-edge lines, and single solid yellow lines as left-edge lines on divided highways. If you see the reverse — yellow on your right and white on your left — you are travelling in the wrong direction.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Passing lanes are separated by broken white lines, not identified by edge-line colours.
Exit ramps are marked with continuity lines, which are wider than regular lane lines.
Divided highways carry one-way traffic on each roadway.

question: What are continuity lines, and where would you see them?
choices: Wider-than-normal lines painted at entry and exit ramps, showing the separation between the through lane and the ramp
Double yellow lines painted through an intersection
The lines that mark a pedestrian crosswalk
The lines that mark parking spaces along a street
explanation: Continuity lines are painted on the highway at entry and exit ramps. They indicate the separation between the through lane and the entry or exit ramps, and they are wider than regular lane-separation lines.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Centre lines are not usually carried through an intersection.
Crosswalks are marked with transverse bars.
Parking spaces are marked separately and are not continuity lines.

question: In which situation do the rules about solid and broken lines NOT apply?
choices: When a vehicle is entering or leaving the highway at a place other than an intersection
When you are running late
When there is no oncoming traffic
When the vehicle ahead is travelling below the speed limit
explanation: The rules respecting solid and broken lines do not apply when a vehicle is entering or leaving the highway at a place other than an intersection; when a vehicle is completing a passing manoeuvre begun in accordance with the rules; when the lines are not clearly visible; or when it is reasonable or prudent to drive to the left of the lines because of weather or other conditions.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Being late is never a listed exception to any rule of the road.
An empty road does not suspend the markings.
A slow vehicle ahead does not create a right to cross a solid line.

question: A single solid yellow line marks the centre of a highway. What does it permit?
choices: Passing in either direction when traffic, sight distance and other conditions are ideal
No passing in either direction under any circumstances
Passing only from the right-hand side
Parking along the centre of the road
explanation: A single solid yellow line marking the centre of a highway permits passing in either direction when traffic, sight distance, and other conditions are ideal. This is different from a DOUBLE solid yellow line, which you may not cross to pass in either direction.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: That is the double solid yellow line.
Passing is done to the left of the vehicle you are overtaking on a two-lane road.
Pavement markings do not authorise parking.

question: Which markings tell you that passing with care is permitted in both directions?
choices: A grey road surface with a single dashed yellow line running down the middle.
A grey road surface with two continuous yellow lines running down the middle.
A grey road surface with one continuous yellow line and, beside it, a dashed yellow line.
A grey road surface with a dashed white line between two lanes and solid white edge lines.
explanation: A broken yellow centre line on a two-lane, two-way road permits passing with care in both directions. The broken line faces both directions of travel equally.
incorrectChoiceExplanations: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing in both directions.
Where one line is solid and one broken, only the traffic beside the broken line may pass.
White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction, so they are not centre-line markings at all.
